title: Eat Cake
description_html:
You're given an array where 0 represents an empty spot, 1 represents a person, and 2 represents a cake.

The distance is defined as the number of empty spots between a person and a cake (not the index difference).

For a given array, what's the shortest distance between any person and any cake?

Examples

[1, 0, 2] → 1
[1, 1, 2] → 0

Follow-up

Assume each person always goes for the closest cake. Given a person's index, return which cake they would end up eating. You don't need to handle conflicts (multiple people going for the same cake) or ties (one person equidistant to multiple cakes).

Approach hint

1D nearest-of-type: two-pass scan. Forward pass tracks the last cake index seen (or +∞); for each person, candidate distance is i − lastCake − 1. Backward pass does the symmetric thing. Take the min per person, then the global min across persons.

For the follow-up: store both the nearest-left-cake-index and nearest-right-cake-index per person; the chosen cake is whichever is closer (ties → either).

Patterns: LC 821 (Shortest Distance to a Character) is the direct analog with the off-by-one distance tweak; LC 849 (Maximize Distance to Closest Person) is the max-distance sibling; LC 1769 (Min Ops to Move Balls) is the per-index distance-sum sibling.
